title: Count distributes additively over append
statement: For any element a and lists l1, l2 over Nat, the number of times a occurs in the concatenation of l1 and l2 equals the sum of how many times a occurs in l1 and how many times it occurs in l2.

formal.statement: theorem List.count_append : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : List.{0} AxNat) -> ((x2 : List.{0} AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (List.count x0 (List.append AxNat x1 x2)) (AxNat.add (List.count x0 x1) (List.count x0 x2)))))

evidence.supports: List.count_append is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.

notes: Induction on l1 (a, l2 fixed). Same shape as bridge::declare_length_append's induction, but count's cons case carries an extra Bool.rec on Nat.beq head a that length's does not, so the step needs the same Or-based case split declare_count_to_multiset already built -- unlike that proof, no Nat.beq_comm flip is needed here, because both sides of the goal split on the exact same beq head a term.
